column1: # arm-poses.csv - named whole-arm poses for the Emre Kalem arm
# !! BOTH ROWS BELOW ARE STALE AS OF 2026-08-08. DO NOT DRIVE THEM. !!
# The arm was DISASSEMBLED- recalibrated and rewired between 2026-08-06 and
# 2026-08-08- and the signal leads were moved at the Uno header. Joint IDs still
# name the same physical joints- but the commanded-angle to mechanical-angle
# mapping did not survive- and neither did these two rows. Specifically:
#   storage asks for J3 = 64. The elbow was re-locked 0-30 on 2026-08-08- so 64
#   now CLAMPS at 30. Driving storage today folds the shoulder and leaves the
#   forearm standing straight up- which is not a storage pose. Confirmed on the
#   bench 2026-08-08 ~21:40: every other axis reached its storage value and the
#   arm did not collapse.
# THREE MORE CLAIMS IN THIS HEADER ARE NOW FALSE- left in place below so the
# reasoning stays readable- but corrected here:
#   "J0 IS ABSENT FROM EVERY ROW ON PURPOSE. Its servo is dead" - the replacement
#   was fitted and J0 was re-locked 0-180 home 90 on 2026-08-08. It drives. Note
#   also the 2026-08-08 no-motion on J0 was NOT a dead servo: there was no 5 V
#   reaching the servos at all. Poses written from now on SHOULD carry j0_deg
#   the console's SAVE POSE button emits that column.
#   "As of 2026-08-06 evening the gripper does not articulate" - it articulates.
#   Proven 2026-08-08 ~20:45 by opposite-direction prong fringing and the gear
#   teeth in a new rotational position. It is still NOT controllable: it does not
#   return to the same finger position for the same commanded angle. See
#   Calibration_Notes/evidence/2026-08-08_J6-retry/.
#   The camera framing every "camera_verified" here was taken against no longer
#   exists - the camera has moved twice since. All three historical ROIs fail a
#   backdrop negative control. See Documentation/2026-08-08-EVENING-SESSION-FINDINGS.md.
# WHAT TO DO: reteach the joints (find real ends- back off- write joint-limits.csv)
# and then re-record these poses from scratch with the console's SAVE POSE button-
# which fills entry_path from the driven teach table. Supersede these rows- do not
# edit them: an old row stays true as of its date.
# WHAT THIS FILE IS. joint-limits.csv says how far each joint MAY go. This file
# says where the arm should BE for a named purpose - storage- pick-approach- and
# so on. Every row here was driven on the real arm and photographed- not planned
# on paper.
# WHY THE ENTRY PATH IS A COLUMN AND NOT A COMMENT. The endpoint is not enough.
# Two poses can both be safe while the straight line between them drives the claw
# through the bench- the wire loom- or the base housing. entry_path records the
# waypoint sequence that was actually driven and observed to be clear- joint by
# joint- in order. TO LEAVE A POSE- REVERSE ITS OWN ENTRY PATH. Do not
# interpolate between two poses in this file and assume the middle is clear.
# NO POSE HERE IS SELF-SUPPORTING. Every one is held by servo torque alone. The
# instant the holder daemon stops or the rocker goes off- all five live joints
# detach together and the arm falls from wherever it is. A pose can only be
# chosen to make that fall SHORT and to keep it away from the loom and the bench
# edge - it can never prevent it. Support the forearm by hand before switching
# off. See .claude/skills/arm-bench-safety/SKILL.md.
# J0 IS ABSENT FROM EVERY ROW ON PURPOSE. Its servo is dead and the joint is
# deliberately left detached- so no pose commands it. Its replacement was ordered
# 2026-08-06 and J0 must be re-measured when fitted - a new horn seats on a
# different spline tooth- so the old 29-110 will not point where it used to.
# J6 ANGLES ARE COMMANDED- NOT ACTUAL. As of 2026-08-06 evening the gripper does
# not articulate: the firmware ramps D11 correctly and the fingers do not move.
# Operator's diagnosis after checking it by hand - the gear is slipping on the
# motor shaft. Any j6_deg below is what the joint was TOLD- and should not be
# read as a finger position until the mechanical fault is fixed and re-verified.
# ANGLES ARE COMMANDED SOFT-LIMIT DEGREES- the same units as joint-limits.csv.
# Nothing in this system observes an output shaft- so "verified" in this file
# means a camera confirmed the arm MOVED and reached a photographed pose - never
# that a shaft is at a measured angle. The camera is uncalibrated
# is derived from pixels.
# DIRECTION MAPPING - HARD-WON- AND ONE OF THEM I GOT BACKWARDS FIRST
#   J1 shoulder  HIGHER = folds over ONTO THE BASE.  LOWER = reaches OUT.
#                Read from pixel height alone this looks inverted- because the
#                claw RISES in frame as the arm folds onto the base. A flat
#                camera projection cannot tell rising from folding. The operator
#                called it correctly from the 3D geometry and the projection did
#                not. When the two disagree- the operator wins.
#   J3 elbow     HIGHER = folded and tucked in.  LOWER = extended out.
#                Re-test this after any large J1 change: with the shoulder laid
#                over- the frame of reference has rotated ~87 degrees and the
#                screen direction of an elbow move is not what it was.
# Do not put a comma inside any field. Use a semicolon or a dash.
